Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The study uses a combination of BioID (proximity labeling) and AP-MS to identify interactors, and pulse-SILAC to identify substrates (degradome). While the study focuses on ubiquitin ligases, it does not use ubiquitin-remnant enrichment (diGly/K-GG) but rather measures protein stability changes via SILAC.

scope: Using BioID and affinity purification–mass spectrometry approaches, we demonstrated that seven WD40 proteins can be considered DCAFs with a high confidence level.

One to two micrograms of total protein was incubated with 20 μl of GFP-trap agarose beads from Chromatek for 3 h at 4 °C. We then washed the beads in lysis buffer and transferred them to a low-bind tube prior to processing for mass spectrometry (MS).

High-performance streptavidin beads (Cytiva; #17511301) were added and incubated overnight at 4 °C under rotation with 1 to 2 mg of total protein then washed once with 1 ml of wash buffer (50 mM Tris–HCl, pH 7.5, 2% SDS) and three times with 1 ml lysis buffer.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The study utilizes multiple proteomics workflows. The interactome was determined via affinity purification (GFP-trap) and proximity labeling (BioID/streptavidin beads), both of which result in purified protein complexes. While pulse-SILAC was also used on lysates to measure degradation, the core sample-scope for the interactomics described is affinity-purified.
